approved: Treasury Laws Amendment (Business Registries Stabilisation and Uplift) Bill 2026

Presented Selection of Bills Committee Report No. 6 of 2026, recommending immediate referrals of four bills to legislative committees with reporting dates from 17 June to 6 August 2026. Moved amendments referring the National Disability Insurance Scheme Amendment (Securing the NDIS for Future Generations) Bill 2026 to inquiry and excluding the Competition and Consumer Amendment (Responding to Exceptional Circumstances) Bill 2026 from referral.

Declared that Appropriation Bill (No. 1) 2026-2027, Appropriation Bill (No. 2) 2026-2027 and Appropriation (Parliamentary Departments) Bill (No. 1) 2026-2027 stood referred to the Federation Chamber immediately, with Treasury Laws Amendment (Business Registries Stabilisation and Uplift) Bill 2026 referred at the adjournment of its second reading debate.

Supported the Treasury Laws Amendment (Business Registries Stabilisation and Uplift) Bill 2026 and said the coalition would not oppose it in the House so a Senate inquiry could examine director ID privacy protections, strict liability offences and ASIC's regulatory direction.

Argued that the bill would prevent legacy provisions from transferring business registry responsibility from ASIC to a body created for a cancelled program, support ASIC's digital and registry powers, protect directors' addresses, link director IDs to company records, and keep RegistryConnect on track.
